text:
tay: Quick sync: policy engine needs to distinguish soft constraints (penalties) vs hard constraints (filters). today everything is a penalty and we had a tenant hit a dedicated-only rule and still got routed to a shared node. that's bad. thoughts on adding an explicit pre-filter stage?

anish: +1. we already compute per-candidate attributes; inserting a cheap pre-filter that rejects hard-constraint failures will be O(n) extra checks and saves later compute. keep hard constraint checks boolean and short-circuit.

rachel: caution: some "hard" constraints are actually preference-like for older tenants. we need a migration plan: introduce constraint types: HARD, SOFT, SOFT_STRICT (soft but with stronger clamp). default mapping: legacy flags -> SOFT for 30d, then q to team to bump to HARD.

liam: implementation detail: router pipeline should be: 1) candidate gather, 2) hard-filter (drop candidates), 3) baseline scoring (apply compile-time transforms), 4) penalty layering (tenant/tier/region penalties), 5) tie-break. tie-break needs to be deterministic but unbiased. proposal: score + small deterministic jitter derived from request-id hash and transform-version.

priya: operational invariants: (a) any hard-filter decision must be auditable (reason code), (b) filters must be cached per-request-window to avoid repeated evaluation in multi-stage routing, (c) a fail-open mode for control-plane outages. also add a circuit-breaker if hard-filter removes >90% of candidates - fallback to relaxed mode and page oncall.

anish: agree on auditable reasons. we should attach an enum reason code and a short text. example: HARD_FILTER_FAILURE_GPU_COMPAT, HARD_FILTER_FAILURE_REGION_RESTRICT. Keep codes stable.

policy-bot: policy-audit: new filter enums added to schema v3. candidate_drop events will be emitted to telemetry with fields: candidate_id, reason_code, route_ts.

tay: tie-break specifics: we want deterministic selection when scores equal-ish. compute tie_score = score + jitter where jitter = (hash(request_id, transform_v) % 1000) / 1e6. jitter in [0, 0.001). ensures reproducible ordering without changing score distribution.

rachel: about penalties: clamp global penalty multiplier to [0.5, 2.0]. don't let tenant-level boosts exceed 1.2 by default. have policy-admin feature to request exceptions with audit trail.

liam: on rollout: add feature-flagged path. plan: create schema, unit tests, e2e in staging with synthetic candidates, then canary on 5% traffic for 24h measuring: candidate_drop_rate, route_win_rate_shift, latency_p95 change, and tenant-error-rate. rollback if candidate_drop_rate jumps >2x baseline or tenant-error-rate increases >0.1%.

priya: caching notes: route_descriptor key should include transform_v and filter_v. sample cache-key: "model|filter_v|transform_v|region_cohort". invalidation happens when we bump either version. TTLs default 60s for control-plane driven descriptors and 5s for sidecar hints.

anish: telemetry collection: emit both pre-filter candidate count and post-filter candidates. log top-3 drop reasons per-route per-minute to help tune. also emit gate-open metric when circuit-breaker engages.

tay: security/audit: all hard-filter definitions must be tied to policy rules with owner. owner approves exceptions. admin UI should show recent hard-filter rejections for a tenant with drilldown.

liam: quick pseudocode for router pipeline we can copy to RFC:

```go
candidates := gather()
allowed := []Candidate{}
for _, c := range candidates {
  if failsHardFilters(c, req) {
    emitDrop(c, reason)
    continue
  }
  allowed = append(allowed, c)
}
if len(allowed) == 0 {
  if controlPlaneUnhealthy() { // fail-open
    allowed = candidates // temporary fallback
    emitMetric("hard_filter_fail_open")
  } else {
    return errorNoCandidates()
  }
}
scored := scoreCandidates(allowed, route_descriptor, sidecar_hints)
winner := pickTopWithDeterministicJitter(scored, req.id, route_descriptor.transform_v)
return winner
```

priya: looks good. include audit event for fail-open so ops can see why fallback happened.

rachel: final point: keep the policy schema backwards compatible by versioning enums. treat missing filter_v as v0 (legacy permissive).

tay: ok action items: tay to draft RFC for hard-filter stage + schema v3, rachel to prepare migration plan for legacy flags, anish to prototype deterministic jitter util, liam to add tests to router service, priya to design audit metrics dashboard. i'll open RFC by EOD and tag @policy-team and @eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:
